title: What Is THCV?
seoTitle: What Is THCV? Meet a Rare Cannabinoid | Uforia Dispensary
description: THCV is a lesser-known cannabinoid closely related to THC. Learn how it differs, where it comes from, what people report and what research has yet to show.
lede: THCV is one of the cannabinoids people start asking about once they read labels closely. It shares part of its name with THC, but it is its own compound, with its own story.

sections.heading: A close relative of THC
sections.html:
THCV stands for tetrahydrocannabivarin. Chemically, it looks a lot like THC, with one notable difference: a shorter tail, the chain of carbon atoms on one end of the molecule. THC's tail has five carbon atoms, while THCV's has three. That small change seems to affect how the compound interacts with the body's endocannabinoid system.

THCV also starts out differently. Most cannabinoids trace back to a compound called CBGA, but THCV comes from a close cousin, CBGVA. In the living plant it exists mostly as an acid, THCVA, which converts to THCV with heat. Our guide to THCA explains how that conversion works.

The "V" in the name comes from "varin," the term chemists use for this family of shorter-tailed cannabinoids. CBDV and CBGV belong to the same family.

sections.heading: Where THCV shows up
sections.html:
In most cannabis, THCV appears only in small amounts. Some strains carry more, and these are often linked to plant lines with roots in southern Africa and parts of Asia. Breeders have also been developing cultivars that produce more of it.

Because it is less common, THCV is usually something you spot on a lab report rather than on the front of a package. When a product has been tested for it, you will see it listed alongside THC, CBD and other cannabinoids.

sections.heading: What people say about it
sections.html:
Some people describe THCV as feeling clearer or more energetic than THC, and some report that its effects seem shorter. Lab and animal research suggests THCV may act differently depending on the amount: in small amounts it may partly block the receptor THC acts on, while in larger amounts it may activate it. Experiences also vary from person to person, and because THCV rarely appears on its own, it can be hard to tell which compound is behind a particular feeling.

You may also see THCV promoted with catchy nicknames tied to appetite or energy. Be cautious with those. Most of the research behind them is early, much of it done in animals or small groups of people, and more research is needed before anyone can make promises about what THCV does.

sections.heading: How to approach THCV
sections.html:
If you are curious, approach THCV the way you would any unfamiliar cannabinoid:

  • Read the full label or lab results, since THCV usually appears alongside THC.
  • Remember that a product with THCV can still be intoxicating, especially if it also contains THC.
  • Pay attention to the product type, since edibles, vapes and flower each feel different and take different amounts of time to kick in.
  • Start low and go slow, and give yourself time to notice how you feel.
  • Keep simple notes so you can compare experiences over time.

takeaways: THCV is a cannabinoid closely related to THC, with a shorter carbon tail.
Most cannabis contains only small amounts, though some strains carry more.
Some people report it feels clearer or shorter-lasting, but research is still early.
Products with THCV often contain THC too, so start low and go slow.
